sections.title: LinkedIn Post
sections.body:
Good design decisions usually happen before the final draft is published.

A simple planning process can make the work clearer:

1. Collect references to define the visual direction.
2. Sketch alternatives instead of settling on the first idea.
3. Review the draft before publishing to catch gaps and refine the result.

The value is in the sequence. References provide direction, alternatives create room for comparison, and review gives the work one final quality check.

A polished outcome often starts with a disciplined process, not a last-minute adjustment.
sections.cta: Save this three-step process for your next design project.
